study: Rutherford et al. 2014, ST Math (MIND Research Institute)
eval_evidence: IES grant to UC Irvine; 'This article is a product of the evaluation conducted by [Farkas & Duncan], without oversight from MIND.' (Caveat: MIND staff S. Schneider/M.E. Martinez are co-authors, a partial developer stake, but the impact evaluation is explicitly framed as developer-independent.)
developer_evidence: A 4-to-5-hr PD on how to use the software 'was provided to all study teachers' plus 1st-year technical support; the report does not specify whether MIND, the districts, or the eval team ran the session.
cascade_evidence: Source/route of the brief software-use training to teachers not specified (observers were trained by MIND staff, but teacher-PD delivery route is not stated).
counterfactual_evidence: Control = no ST Math (off-grade same-school comparison); business-as-usual math instruction.
coaching_evidence: Only a 4-5 hr training session plus 1st-year technical support; no ongoing in-class coaching of teachers reported.
student_dose_evidence: ST Math is a supplemental computer-assisted math software used ~2x45 min/week in the computer lab — a substantial student-facing software dose beyond regular instruction.
maturity_evidence: Primary confirmatory effect is the 1-year main effect (end of first implementation year); report notes students 'new to the districts for their school's 1st year'.
